key_insight: Machine learning can diagnose degradation mechanisms in simulated lead-free solar cells from temperature- and illumination-dependent voltage measurements, but generalization depends strongly on training coverage.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support post-fabrication fault diagnosis, while simulations suggest replacing Spiro-OMeTAD with CuI raises efficiency from 19.6% to 21.6%, mainly through fill-factor gains.
method: Generate approximately 42,000 SCAPS-1D simulations of RbSn₀.₅Ge₀.₅I₃ solar cells.
Compare surrogate regression trained on factorial grids versus Latin hypercube sampling.
Use multi-label classification to identify six degradation mechanisms from temperature- and illumination-dependent open-circuit voltage.
evidence_signal: Diagnostic macro F1 reached 0.938 versus 0.687 for a calibrated physics-rule baseline; regression R² fell from 0.9997 on held-out grid points to 0.58 on independently sampled devices, while Latin hypercube training achieved 0.995.
watch_item: Results are simulation-based, and the diagnostic classifier fails to generalize to mechanism combinations absent from training.
paper_title: Interpretable machine learning diagnosis of degradation mechanisms in lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells from temperature- and illumination-dependent electrical measurements
